## Yuri and Yurilu Falls: a separate river journey in Canaima

**Yuri and Yurilu (Yuri–Yuri Lu)** are in Venezuela's Canaima National Park area. Unlike the enormous drop of [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), the main attractions here are river cascades, rocky shores and tropical plants beside the water. Visiting them is another way to discover Canaima's nature after exploring the lagoon and principal waterfalls.

The journey to Yuri and Yurilu is best considered an optional excursion on a free day. It requires separate transport arrangements and assessment of access conditions, so it should not be treated as a short stop right beside a tourist lodge.

## What are Yuri and Yurilu like?

In the Guiana Highlands, rivers flow across rocky channels and through forest. These cascades differ from water plunging off a gigantic plateau: visitors observe several streams, water flowing between stones and the riverbank at close range.

The name **Yuri–Yuri Lu** refers to related waterfall sites. Variants such as Yuri, Yuri Lu and Yurilu appear in excursion descriptions. On some local itineraries, the second cascade is accessible only at suitable water levels, so a description promising “two waterfalls” should be checked against conditions on the day.

Published travel accounts give differing heights and distances between cascades. For practical planning, it is more useful to establish the actual route, walking approach and safety conditions than to rely on unverified figures.

## Getting there from Canaima

Excursions depart from Canaima's tourist area, but transport and the order of stages vary. One described local itinerary uses a vehicle across the savanna to Puerto Verde, a curiara boat to cross the Carrao River and a walk to the falls. This is an example from another operator, not a standard arrangement for every Ada Tours excursion.

Before booking, confirm how the ground transfer works, whether a boat is included, how long the walk will be and whether both cascades can be visited. These details depend on the season and current river conditions.

If your journey already includes the long river expedition to Angel Falls, schedule Yuri and Yurilu for another day. Transport in Canaima depends on water and weather; delays are particularly inconvenient before a domestic flight.

## How Yuri and Yurilu differ from other waterfalls

Canaima has many kinds of water scenery. If you have limited time, comparing the destinations will help you choose what interests you most.

| Place | Main feature |
|---|---|
| Yuri and Yurilu | River cascades |
| [Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) | A path behind the water curtain |
| [Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) | Waterfall beside the lagoon |
| [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) | Remote, towering waterfall |

[Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) and [Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) are normally explored together with [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/). Yuri and Yurilu offer a separate river outing. Travelers who prefer uphill walks and mountain panoramas can choose another free-day option: [Kurevaina tepui](/venezuela/place/kuravaina-tepui/).

None of these sites fully substitutes for another. Although all lie in the same national park, their actual excursions differ in travel, duration and physical demands.

## Can this excursion be added to a four-day journey?

Yes, if your itinerary has a free day and local conditions allow the trip. On the [four-day Ada Tours “Venezuelan Beauty: Canaima and Angel Falls” tour](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/), day three is reserved for relaxation by the lagoon and optional activities. These include a separately charged Yuri–Yuri Lu excursion.

Ada Tours also offers a standalone [Yuri and Yurilu waterfalls excursion](/venezuela/yuri-yurilu-falls/yuri-yurilu-waterfalls-trip/). Its exact duration, transport, guiding and sequence of stops are agreed when booking. A description of a natural site does not establish what is included in the excursion product.

On a short journey, first check which waterfalls are already included in the basic tour, then choose an additional outing. Compare the options in our [Venezuela tours catalog](/venezuela/tour/).

## Water levels, trails and equipment

During the rainy season, the cascades can carry more water, but high water can also complicate boat crossings and access to particular areas. Wet stones require care in any season. A date on the calendar alone cannot guarantee that both falls will be accessible.

Bring shoes with non-slip soles, quick-drying clothing, a rain jacket and waterproof protection for electronics. Sun protection and insect repellent are useful on open sections. If the excursion involves swimming, it must be explicitly agreed with the guide and comply with local safety rules.

For children and travelers who find uneven ground difficult, confirm the walking section in advance. The physical demands cannot be judged from photographs of waterfalls alone.

## Frequently asked questions about Yuri and Yurilu

### Where are Yuri and Yurilu Falls?

In the Canaima National Park area of Bolívar state, Venezuela. Excursions are organized from Canaima's tourist area.

### Can I see both falls on one outing?

The combined option is offered under the name Yuri–Yuri Lu. Visiting both depends on the chosen itinerary, weather and water levels; confirm the details for your travel date.

### Are Yuri and Yurilu included in the main Angel Falls tour?

On the [four-day Ada Tours itinerary](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/), Yuri and Yurilu are a separately paid optional excursion on a free day.

### What should I choose on a free day in Canaima?

For another nature journey along the water, consider Yuri and Yurilu. If trekking with views over savanna and plateau appeals more, explore the [Kurevaina excursion](/venezuela/kuravaina-tepui/venezuela-kuravaina-trekking/). The choice depends on weather, fitness and available time.

## Yuri and Yurilu Falls: an optional Canaima excursion

[Yuri and Yurilu](/venezuela/place/yuri-yurilu-falls/) are two waterfalls in the Canaima area where water forms broad cascades amid rocky banks and vegetation. This landscape differs from the great height of Angel Falls: the focus is on flowing water, nearby rock formations and forested surroundings.

Our collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} to which the falls can be added as a separate outing. On the [four-day “Venezuelan Beauty” tour](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/), they **are not included in the mandatory activities of the first two sightseeing days**. They are one option for the free third day.

We offer the standalone [“Canaima: Yuri and Yurilu Waterfalls Excursion”](/venezuela/yuri-yurilu-falls/yuri-yurilu-waterfalls-trip/). The commercial itinerary also uses the name Yuri–Yuri Lu. These are names for one optional product, not two independently charged waterfall tours.

## How the excursion fits into the main itinerary

On the first day, travelers fly from Caracas to Canaima and visit [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/) and Hacha and Sapo waterfalls. The following day involves a full river expedition to [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) along the [Carrao](/venezuela/place/carrao-river/) and [Churún](/venezuela/place/churun-river/), followed by an overland hike to a viewpoint.

Day three is reserved for relaxation by the lagoon, walking, kayaking and optional excursions. **Yuri and Yurilu are an option on this free day.** The schedule, transport and guiding for the separate outing are agreed on booking; without these details, it would be wrong to promise a specific departure time or walking duration.

The final, fourth day involves a return to Caracas. Scheduling a new excursion to Yuri and Yurilu in place of the return flight is not part of the main itinerary without changing the full program.

## Yuri–Yuri Lu price: 89 USD

On the four-day tour, the **additional trip to Yuri and Yurilu costs 89 USD**. It is charged on top of the basic trip price.

The basic program includes Caracas–Canaima–Caracas flights, 3 nights in a lodge, meals on the specified days, the Angel Falls excursion, Hacha and Sapo waterfalls, and other included services. The Canaima National Park fee of 40 USD is also paid separately.

The Yuri–Yuri Lu price applies to this particular program. If another tour offers a similar outing, check its own services and current conditions. The standalone product's public description does not specify an exact duration, transport type or guide language; these details are confirmed before booking.

## Yuri and Yurilu, Pozo Azul or Kurevaina: choosing an outing

A free day offers several distinct experiences with different physical demands.

| Optional excursion | Price on this tour |
|---|---:|
| [Yuri and Yurilu](/venezuela/yuri-yurilu-falls/yuri-yurilu-waterfalls-trip/) | **89 USD** |
| [Pozo Azul](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/canaima-blue-lagoon-trip/) | **88 USD** |
| [Kurevaina and Pozo Azul](/venezuela/kuravaina-tepui/venezuela-kuravaina-trekking/) | **125 USD** |

Yuri and Yurilu are well suited to exploring river cascades and rocky banks. Pozo Azul offers a comparatively gentle nature outing to a small pool. The [Kurevaina](/venezuela/place/kuravaina-tepui/) option adds a more substantial hike with views over savanna and tepuis.

The prices are close enough that the experience and physical demands matter more. **Listing all three as optional activities does not mean their schedules can automatically be combined into one free day.** Multiple outings require separate confirmation of timing.

## Nature and visiting rules

Canaima is known for rocky tepui plateaus, rivers and waterfalls. The national park is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Moving near water requires care: stones may be slippery, and currents and water levels change.

Use permitted routes, avoid approaching cascade edges without the guide's direction and protect vegetation. Swimming near waterfalls cannot be promised solely on the basis of a place name: the possibility and safety must be confirmed when arranging the excursion.

If your main purpose is to see Angel Falls, the [four-day tour](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) already includes a trip there. Yuri and Yurilu broaden your experience of Canaima's rivers and nature rather than replacing the principal excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about Yuri and Yurilu

### Are Yuri and Yurilu included in the price of the four-day tour?

No. The Yuri–Yuri Lu excursion costs an additional **89 USD**.

### On which day can we visit the falls?

On the [“Venezuelan Beauty” itinerary](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/), day three is free for optional outings in Canaima. The exact departure time is agreed on booking.

### Does the outing replace the Angel Falls excursion?

No. Angel Falls is part of the main itinerary on day two; Yuri and Yurilu offer an optional extension to the trip.

### Can Yuri and Yurilu be combined with trekking to Kurevaina?

The public four-day itinerary lists them as separate free-day options. Combining them, the timing and cost must be agreed individually; no automatically bundled product is advertised.

## Pozo Azul excursions in Canaima: Blue Lagoon or trekking

[Pozo Azul](/venezuela/place/pozo-azul-canaima/), or the Blue Pool, lies amid Canaima's natural landscapes in Venezuela. Water collects in a small natural pool surrounded by stones and vegetation. Its color changes with light, water levels and the condition of the bottom.

This place is suited to a relaxed introduction to [Canaima National Park](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), but it can also become one stop on a more physically active hike. Ada Tours offers **two different excursions** involving Pozo Azul. They differ in exertion, walking route and purpose.

## A separate walk to the Blue Lagoon

The [“Blue Lagoon: Pozo Azul in Canaima” excursion](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/canaima-blue-lagoon-trip/) focuses on the pool itself. Travelers walk among greenery and relax by the water. It is a choice for those who want time in nature without a scheduled climb up a tepui.

The price is **$88 on the 2027 “Venezuelan Beauty” itinerary**. This amount applies to that particular tour option and cannot automatically be used for other journeys or additional service packages.

The walking section and trail conditions must be confirmed for the actual date. Swimming depends on the local guide's permission and water conditions, not on a photograph of a clear pool.

## Trekking to Kurevaina tepui with Pozo Azul

The [“Kurevaina Tepui Trek and Pozo Azul” excursion](/venezuela/kuravaina-tepui/venezuela-kuravaina-trekking/) is a more active walk. The route combines savanna, a forest trail, a stop at Pozo Azul and an ascent of [Kurevaina tepui](/venezuela/place/kuravaina-tepui/). From higher ground, travelers enjoy views of table mountains and green valleys.

Choose this for the walking and elevated panoramas. It is more demanding than visiting the pool as a separate nature stop. On the 2027 trip, the option costs **$125**. Duration, schedule and specific included services are determined when booking.

| Format | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Blue Lagoon | Pool and nature walk |
| Kurevaina + Pozo Azul | Trail, ascent and panoramas |

## How this part of Canaima differs from Angel Falls

Canaima National Park, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, covers a vast area in southeastern Venezuela. It is famous for tepuis, rivers and waterfalls, including the world's highest, [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/).

Pozo Azul offers a different natural scene, with a small pool and a walk through vegetation. The [full-day river excursion to Angel Falls](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/) follows the Carrao and Churún, stopping near Ratonsito and the Laime viewpoint. It cannot be considered an ordinary continuation of the Blue Lagoon route.

If you want several different landscapes, first check how much time your main tour spends in Canaima and which excursions are included. A visit to a single pool does not replace a long river expedition.

## What to consider before walking

Canaima's humid tropical conditions combine with changeable river levels. Rain can make trails and water approaches slippery, so shoes with good grip are useful. Take insect repellent, drinking water and waterproof protection for electronics.

On the trekking route, you need to be able to climb over uneven terrain. If your goal is quiet relaxation by a pool, the shorter excursion is more appropriate than hiking to a summit just to include a stop at Pozo Azul.

Local conservation rules and guides' instructions take priority over independently choosing a trail or swimming spot. Weather changes conditions; no published photograph guarantees that the pool will look the same during your visit.

## Frequently asked questions about Pozo Azul

### Are Pozo Azul and Angel Falls the same place?

No. [Pozo Azul](/venezuela/place/pozo-azul-canaima/) is a small natural pool, while [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) is a gigantic waterfall deeper in the park. They have separate excursion routes.

### Can I visit Pozo Azul without ascending a tepui?

Yes. Our selection includes a [standalone excursion to the Blue Lagoon](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/canaima-blue-lagoon-trip/).

### Is there an option for active travelers?

Yes. The [Kurevaina trek](/venezuela/kuravaina-tepui/venezuela-kuravaina-trekking/) includes Pozo Azul and an ascent of the table mountain.

### Is swimming included?

The destination description does not guarantee swimming. Entering the water is subject to the guide's decision and current visiting conditions.

## Ratonsito Island: an excursion to Angel Falls along the Churún River

[Ratonsito](/venezuela/place/ratoncito-island/) is a small river island in Canaima National Park. It is part of the route toward [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/): here one stretch of the Churún River journey ends and the walk to the Laime viewpoint begins.

For travelers, Ratonsito is primarily part of **a river-and-hiking excursion**, not a beach resort island in its own right. The journey changes here: after the motorized canoe, a forest trail awaits, while the sheer walls of Auyán-tepui and the towering Angel Falls draw closer.

## How the Ada Tours one-day excursion works

On the [“Angel Falls in One Day: Carrao and Churún Rivers, Ratonsito and Laime” itinerary](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/), travelers first take a ground transfer to a river landing, then ride traditional motorized Indigenous canoes along the Carrao River. Along the way, there is a savanna walk and a stop at a natural pool called the “Pool of Happiness” in the itinerary.

The boats then enter the narrower Churún River and pass the high rock walls of Devil's Canyon. The route leads to Ratonsito, with a view toward Angel Falls. After stopping, visitors begin **an approximately one-hour walk through humid tropical forest** to the Laime viewpoint.

Lunch and a return to Canaima on the same day are included. The order of stops and navigability of the river can depend on water levels and weather.

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Carrao | Motorized canoe journey |
| Churún | Rock walls and river travel |
| Ratonsito | Stop before the trail |
| Laime | View of Angel Falls |

## What you see on the way to Laime

After disembarking, the route passes through dense vegetation. The forest trail features small reddish and orange streams, large trees, orchids, bromeliads and moss-covered stones. The contrast between the open river and damp forest is especially striking.

The destination is the Laime viewpoint, offering one of the well-known views of Angel Falls. **The waterfall is about 979 m high**, according to Venezuela's national park authority and UNESCO materials. The amount of water, clarity of the sky and visibility of the cliff depend on season and current weather.

A hike is more than a series of scenic views: the path crosses natural soil and stones. Rain can make the trail more slippery and increase walking time.

## Ratonsito or Canaima Lagoon: how excursions differ

“Canaima” refers to both a vast protected natural area and the tourist settlement near the lagoon. Excursions here vary significantly.

The [“Canaima Lagoon: Sapo and Hacha Falls” excursion](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/sapo-hacha-lagoon-trip/) includes a boat ride across the lagoon and walks to nearby waterfalls, including [Sapo](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/). It does not specify the Carrao–Churún journey to Ratonsito. It is therefore not a shorter version of the complete river expedition to Angel Falls.

[Pozo Azul](/venezuela/place/pozo-azul-canaima/) is another separate destination, a small natural pool amid vegetation. It is suitable for a nature walk but does not automatically offer views of Angel Falls.

If the world's highest waterfall is your main goal, choose the excursion that explicitly names the river route to Angel Falls, Ratonsito and the viewpoint.

## Conditions and preparation

The river section depends on water levels: very low or high water can alter the route. Guides determine navigable stretches and safe landing areas. Use the provided safety equipment on the boat and follow the crew's instructions.

For the walk, bring shoes with reliable grip, light rain protection, water and a small bag comfortable to carry through the forest. If you have limits on physical activity, discuss them before choosing the full-day excursion.

Ratonsito lies within a protected area on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Local conservation rules, including respect for Pemón territory, matter throughout the route.

## Frequently asked questions about Ratonsito Island

### Is Ratonsito a separate island for a beach holiday?

No. On our excursion it serves as a river stop on the way to Angel Falls.

### How do visitors reach Ratonsito?

By motorized canoe along the Carrao and Churún rivers, after a ground transfer to the landing stage. The exact timing depends on excursion conditions.

### Is there a walking section?

Yes. After Ratonsito, the [one-day Angel Falls itinerary](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/) includes a forest hike to the Laime viewpoint.

### Can I replace this outing with an excursion to Sapo?

The [Sapo excursion](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/sapo-hacha-lagoon-trip/) covers a different water area and program. It does not replace traveling up the Churún toward Angel Falls.

## Sapo Falls excursion: behind the curtain of water in Canaima

[Sapo Falls](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) attract travelers because of a remarkable way to experience falling water: when river levels permit, guides can lead visitors along a rocky passage **behind the curtain of water**. Instead of looking from a distant bank, you hear the roar of the falls and feel the spray close by.

Sapo is near Canaima Lagoon in the national park of southeastern Venezuela. The excursion normally combines a boat crossing and a walk. For travelers who have come to Canaima for [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), it is a separate experience on a route relatively close to the lagoon.

## What is included in the Ada Tours excursion?

We offer [“Canaima Lagoon: Sapo and Hacha Falls”](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/sapo-hacha-lagoon-trip/). Travelers board a traditional boat, cross the lagoon and visit **two waterfalls: Hacha and Sapo**.

The highlight is the passage behind Sapo's flow. From the rock face, the curtain of water falls directly in front of visitors; the trail gives an unusual view of the cascade. The route then returns to the lodge. The boat ride and both waterfall visits are included; additional services not named in the description should not be assumed.

[Hacha](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/) is another waterfall easily seen on the same excursion. It should not be confused with Sapo: even when both are visited consecutively, the approach and access arrangements differ.

## When can you pass behind the waterfall?

Access to the rocky passage is determined by **water levels, weather and the local guide's assessment**. During heavy flow, the section may be closed even when the rest of the excursion takes place. Thus, the passage behind the curtain describes a possible activity, not a promise that it will be available in all weather.

Stones near the waterfall are wet, slippery and frequently covered in spray. Wear shoes with good grip and follow the group's safe route. Protect your camera or phone from water in advance.

If the passage is temporarily inaccessible, the guides decide how the visit can proceed. Crossing a closed barrier independently for a photograph is not allowed.

## Sapo and Angel Falls: two different excursions

Angel Falls, famous as the world's highest waterfall, lies on a remote river route through the park. The [one-day Angel Falls excursion](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/) follows the Carrao and Churún rivers, stops near [Ratonsito](/venezuela/place/ratoncito-island/) and includes a hike to the Laime viewpoint.

The Sapo route covers a smaller area, concentrating on the lagoon and two nearby waterfalls. This does not eliminate weather-related risks; it simply avoids the same long expedition deep into the park.

| Site | How the visit works |
|---|---|
| Sapo | Lagoon and trail behind the water curtain |
| Hacha | Lagoon and waterfall visit |
| Angel Falls | Churún/Carrao rivers and forest trail |

Canaima's geography also includes small natural pools such as [Pozo Azul](/venezuela/place/pozo-azul-canaima/). Visiting that pool is a separate excursion product and should not automatically be added to the Sapo–Hacha itinerary.

## Canaima as a natural heritage site

Canaima National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site for its extraordinary table mountains, or tepuis, sheer cliffs and numerous waterfalls. Venezuela's park authority also describes the cultural significance of these landscapes for the Pemón people.

Many local rivers have a dark hue from naturally occurring organic substances, while pale sand and green banks can be seen alongside the water. Waterfalls look different after rain and in drier months, so trail conditions are assessed on site.

Protected-area rules apply even to short excursions. Travelers follow permitted routes with local guides.

## What to bring

Expect wet ground, spray and possible rain. Light clothing, sturdy-soled shoes, waterproof protection for electronics and a dry change of clothes are useful. On the boat, follow the crew's requirements, and on the trail do not overtake the guide near dangerous sections.

If passing **directly behind the waterfall** is particularly important to you, remember that this section depends on natural conditions. The main purpose is to see Sapo and Hacha, not to recreate a photograph from a specific position at any cost.

## Frequently asked questions about Sapo Falls

### Can I walk behind Sapo Falls?

The excursion includes the possibility of doing so, but access depends on water levels and the guide's decision on the day.

### Are Sapo and Hacha visited together?

Yes. The [Ada Tours excursion across Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/sapo-hacha-lagoon-trip/) visits both falls.

### Is the long river route to Angel Falls required?

No. Sapo has a separate lagoon excursion. [Angel Falls](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/) requires a different journey.

### Can I swim at Sapo?

The excursion description does not promise swimming at the falls. Local rules and guides determine whether entering the water is allowed.
